title: About the digitized district register
place_note: State administrative records; statewide scope does not imply complete county coverage.
record_label: ca. 1860–1954, catalog span; compilation date unverified
summary: The accessible scan begins with Broome and ends in Onondaga. It is an excerpt from a bound volume, not a statewide census.
source_locator: B0494, PDF p. 1; foliation through PDF p. 116

title: A 1910 reporting law sends trustees’ reports through local and state offices
place_note: Statewide legal scope; no particular surviving local file asserted.
event_label: Enacted June 23, 1910, before the Capitol fire
record_label: Historic statute in a federal compilation; the office began January 1, 1912.
summary: The law directed district superintendents to retrieve trustees’ annual reports from town clerks, prepare an abstract for the Education Commissioner, and deposit the reports and a copy of the abstract with county clerks. This was a route for annual reports, not a documented trail for district-organization minutes or for a particular reconstructed ledger entry.
source_locator: Laws of 1910, ch. 607 §395(14); federal compilation, printed pp. 51–54
review: Statute checked; local implementation and survival of copies not demonstrated

title: Capitol fire and attempted reconstruction
place_note: Statewide administrative scope; the Capitol fire was in Albany.
record_label: Finding aid describes surviving 1873–1971 legal files
summary: The fire destroyed Education Department district-formation records. B0554 describes efforts to reconstruct them from local records and refers to B0494 for additional reconstruction materials. This does not establish that the fire caused centralization.
source_locator: B0554, subseries 6; date from NYS Library Fire Collection

title: Township-era consolidations and refiling
place_note: Statewide administrative instruction; not a particular district action.
event_label: May 2, 1917 to August 1, 1918 (actions under the township law)
record_label: Instruction's date not verified
summary: The register's procedural note says consolidations under the township law during this interval are void and new papers must be filed. It distinguishes those actions from other consolidations and marks certain divided districts with a star.
source_locator: B0494, PDF p. 2

title: Central rural schools authorized
place_note: Statewide legal scope.
record_label: Later finding aid
summary: New York authorized central rural schools in 1914. The B0554 finding aid reports only one centralization before the legislature authorized added financial aid in 1925.
source_locator: B0554, subseries 1

title: State aid changes the terms of centralization
place_note: Statewide legal scope.
record_label: Later finding aid
summary: New York expanded aid for rural district reorganization, including transportation and school construction. Centralization depended in part on distinct fiscal and institutional arrangements, not on the 1911 fire alone.
source_locator: Certification files finding aid, historical note

title: Statewide Master Plan for School District Reorganization
place_note: Statewide planning scope.
record_label: State Education Department retrospective history
summary: The 1947 plan supplied a statewide pattern for reorganizing districts but was not compulsory. It is context for reading the last years represented in the register extract.
source_locator: Brief history, opening section
